stories.headline: J&K Minister Satish Sharma flags issue of ‘defiance, disrespect’ of bureaucrat with CM Omar Abdullah
stories.deck: Mr. Sharma, who holds several portfolios including Transport, in a letter to the Chief Minister sought the transfer of J&K Transport Commissioner Vishesh Paul Mahajan, who was posted at the position by the Lieutenant-Governor in December 2024
stories.bodyText:
J&K Minister Satish Sharma has flagged the issue of “defiance and disrespect towards the authority of the Ministry”, allegedly displayed by a senior bureaucrat, with Chief Minister Omar Abdullah.
Mr. Sharma, who holds several portfolios including Transport, in a letter to the Chief Minister sought the transfer of J&K Transport Commissioner Vishesh Paul Mahajan, who was posted at the position by the Lieutenant-Governor in December 2024.
“Mr. Mahajan’s continued defiance of and disrespect towards the authority of this Ministry has reached a point where the orderly administration of the Transport Department is being seriously compromised. I regret that I am compelled to raise this matter formally, having exhausted other means of resolving it,” reads the letter of Mr. Sharma.
He said Mr. Mahajan’s conduct has “given rise to open defiance to written or verbal directives, bypassing, discourteous conduct and communication towards the Minister”.
The J&K Minister, in the letter, highlighted that the Transport Commissioner functions as the principal executive officer of the Department under the policy direction and overall supervision of the Minister-in-charge, who in turn remains answerable to the House and to the public for the functioning of the Department.
“Persistent insubordination by a senior officer not only undermines the authority and dignity of the elected office but also disrupts the chain of administrative accountability, adversely affects the morale of the Department, and ultimately impedes the delivery of public services to the citizens,” said the Minister.
The Minister asked the CM to intervene and “requested that Mr Mahajan be immediately moved out of the post of Transport Commissioner and a suitable officer of appropriate seniority be posted in his place”.
The J&K government and the L-G administration have been constantly on a collision course when it comes to transfers of officials in J&K, ever since the elected government took over in October 2024. The elected government and the Centre are yet to finalise the Transaction of Business Rules, which defines the domain of the Chief Minister, Council of Ministers and the L-G in the seven-year-old UT.
Mr. Mahajan earlier served as the Deputy Commissioner, Reasi, and was transferred and appointed as the Director, Tourism, Jammu, by the L-G. However, the Omar Abdullah government had objected to his transfer in 2024 too.

stories.headline: Rajya Sabha row over ‘lungiwala’ comment against MP
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: 
CPM
 MP John Brittas has moved a privilege motion against 
BJP
 MP Sushmita Dev, alleging that she addressed him as “lungiwala” during proceedings in Rajya Sabha Monday. Dev denied that she had cast aspersions on attire of any state.
Brittas raised the issue in the House Wednesday after listed papers were laid on the table at the start of the day. He said a member targeted him with the “lungiwala” remark while he was moving a statutory resolution against the Income Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026, Monday.
Brittas said the MP came from the treasury benches, stood behind him, disturbed him and started calling him a “lungi wala”.
“I’m a proud Indian, South Indian and a proud Malayali... I cherish every moment being a Malayali — our language, culture, cuisine, and of course, our attire,” Brittas said.
Making an observation on the issue, Rajya Sabha Chairperson C P Radhakrishnan said he would call the MPs concerned to his chamber to discuss the matter. He also urged MPs to be careful not to hurt the sentiments and feelings of fellow members.

“Our culture is unique and inclusive of diverse regional cultures. There should be no disrespect to the cultural traditions and regional identities of our colleagues,” he said.
While parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju requested the chair to allow Dev to put her response on record, leader of the House J P Nadda said govt did not subscribe to such statements and respected every state’s attire.
The proceedings were adjourned till 2pm amid the din. Many MPs from south India protested in Parliament complex, shouting “our lungi, our pride” in support of Brittas.
When the House reassembled, Dev sought to clarify her position: “I’m a Bengali from Assam. I have seen different states where we wear different attires, clothes. Neither I nor any member has cast aspersions on any state’s attire....”

stories.headline: Monsoon Session: Rahul Gandhi rejects govt’s offer for discussion on NEET protest
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Increased ruckus hit Lok Sabha Wednesday after govt told opposition home minister 
Amit Shah
 was ready to participate in, and reply to, a discussion on 
NEET protest
 — as BJP’s attempt to break the deadlock that has virtually washed out Parliament’s monsoon session came to a naught on the penultimate day.
LoP 
Rahul Gandhi
 said the country’s younger generation is not interested in Shah’s lecture and imagination, and he should merely tell who ordered use of pellet guns and nail-studded lathis on students.
After repeated adjournments, parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju told LS that Shah has written a letter to the Speaker that a discussion on NEET protest can start immediately, and he would reply. Rijiju urged opposition to sit peacefully for the discussion, saying “the home minister is waiting”.
He said just two days were left in the session while the opposition was running away. But opposition intensified sloganeering and jammed the well. Presiding officer Jagdambika Pal repeatedly said he was ready to start the discussion if the members returned to their seats.
But opposition was in no mood to relent. Rahul told reporters there was no need for a discussion and Shah should simply tell the House “who gave the order to shoot the students, who shot the students, who gave the order to beat the students with nail-studded lathis”, which would establish if he is culpable or incompetent.
Rahul said Shah has been missing from the House for 20 days, even as he came and left Parliament in “30 cars every day”. He claimed there are a thousand cops stationed outside Shah’s residence to ensure no student comes there. “Shah has no courage, his balloon has punctured,” he remarked.
On rejecting Shah’s offer of discussion, Congress’s KC Venugopal said Shah did not come to LS during the day. Deputy LoP Gaurav Gogoi accused him of obfuscating the issue by offering a discussion on NEET protest. “The issue was discussed over two days under the debate on ‘unfair means bill’. Only Shah’s reply is pending.”
Minutes before the proceedings, the Speaker called Venugopal to ask him about opposition’s response to Shah’s offer for a discussion, and was told opposition was sticking to its demand for a statement by Shah and discussion on Ram temple “Chanda Chori”.

stories.headline: Race to post of Odisha DGP hit by controversies
stories.deck: Odisha has forwarded names of 11 IPS officers to UPSC as against three senior most IPS officers laid down procedure in Prakash Singh versus Union Government case
stories.bodyText:
With just four days left for the appointment of a new Director General of Police following the retirement of incumbent DGP Y. B. Khurania, the race for the top policing post in Odisha has never been more controversial.
A public interest litigation seeking adherence to Apex Court laid down procedure in Prakash Singh versus Union Government case on appointment of DGP by the State Government from amongst a panel of three senior-most officers prepared by the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) is already pending in Supreme Court.
It is alleged that the BJP government was trying to bring in an officer from outside the bracket of three senior most IPS officers for the top post. Similarly, in what it seems as shadow fight to favour IPS officers of their choice for the top post, activists have jumped in to filing PIL and sending petitions to Union Home Minister Amit Shah.
Present Odisha DGP, Mr. Khurania, a 1990 batch IPS officer, was appointed as the Head of Police Force of Odisha, on August 16, 2024. After completion of two years, he would demit office on August 16, 2026.
The process of DGP appointment should have been started months before retirement of outgoing DGP. As per Supreme Court’s laid down procedure, the Mohan Majhi Government had sent names of three senior most officers including Sudhanshu Sarangi (1990 batch), Susanta Kumar Nath (1993) and R.P. Koche, (1993) for consideration UPSC.
Before the Commission could take a call on the three names, the State government expanded the list of officers for consideration of UPSC from three to 11 by including eight senior IPS officers from 1994 batch to 1996.
The State government on Monday (August 10, 2026) promoted two 1994-batch officers Sanjeeb Kumar Panda and Yeshwant Kumar Jethwa to the grade of DG of Police. If the list of original three names recommended to UPSC is altered, Mr. Panda and Mr. Jethwa would automatically come into contention.
Senior lawyer and former Home Minister P. Chidambaram has already appeared in PIL arguing that Odisha government violated the Prakash Singh judgment on appointment of DGP. In petition addressed to Mr. Shah, some activists have highlighted controversies surrounding a senior IPS officer who may be considered for the DGP post.

Lok Sabha refers FCRA bill to JPC amid uproar as opposition calls it ‘anti-minority’
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha on Wednesday referred the controversial FCRA bill to a joint parliamentary committee (JPC) amid opposition protests that called the legislation a BJP design to target minorities and demanded it be junked altogether. MPs K C Venugopal, Akhilesh Yadav and T R Baalu spoke for the bill’s withdrawal.
Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill will be scrutinised by the panel comprising LS and RS members, with the deadline for submission of the report being the first week of winter session.
‘Foreign money can’t just be brought to India sans laws’ Congress’s K C Venugopal demanded govt withdraw the FCRA bill. Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said Congress and other parties have demanded important bills should be referred to JPC or other panels, and those opposed to the bill can put their views before JPC.
He said there is no question of targeting any minority community and the bill is designed to bolster national security. He claimed there is a campaign to mislead certain minority communities.
Questioning Rijiju’s claim, SP chief Akhilesh said the minister should name one bill of Modi govt that has not been anti-minority. He asserted entire opposition is against the bill. In retaliation, Rijiju challenged Akhilesh to show one provision in FCRA that is against minorities.

briefs.headline: Punjab CM Mann meets Governor, seeks parole for ex-CM Beant Singh assassination convict Hawara
briefs.deck: Mr. Mann requested the Punjab Governor to consider granting 10 day-parole to Hawara on humanitarian grounds, saying that after 31 years, his ailing mother has a renewed hope of meeting her son
briefs.bodyText:
Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) met Governor Gulab Chand Kataria and sought his intervention for granting parole to Jagtar Singh Hawara, a member of the banned terrorist outfit Babbar Khalsa terrorist, who is serving a life sentence for the 1995 assassination of former Chief Minister Beant Singh.
Mr. Mann requested the Punjab Governor to consider granting 10 day-parole to Hawara on humanitarian grounds, saying that after 31 years, his ailing mother has a renewed hope of meeting her son. The Chief Minister said the matter requires the Governor’s recommendation as the case is being heard in Delhi, while assuring that the Punjab government will take full responsibility for ensuring that law and order is not affected if Hawara is granted parole.
“Jagtar Singh Hawara has been lodged in Jail for the last 31 years. His mother is old and suffering from age-related health issues and is currently semi-conscious. In view of her deteriorating health condition, I have requested the Governor to kindly consider granting 10 days’ parole to Jagtar Singh Hawara at the earliest so that he can meet his mother,” he said.
The Punjab and Haryana High Court, last month had directed Mandoli prison authorities in Delhi, where Hawara is currently lodged, to seek recommendations from the Chandigarh Administration and decide his parole application within a stipulated time frame. In 2007, Hawara was sentenced to death, but in 2010 it was commuted by the High Court. Hawara is serving imprisonment for the rest of his life in connection with the August 31, 1995, blast at the Civil Secretariat in Chandigarh, which killed Beant Singh and 16 others.
Interestingly, in March this year, the Punjab government had written to the Tihar Jail authorities recommending the rejection of the parole application of Hawara.

stories.headline: Karnataka Bandh unlikely to disrupt normal life as most organisations extend only moral support
stories.bodyText:
Normal life is unlikely to be affected on Thursday (August 13) despite the bandh call given by Kannada activist Vatal Nagaraj against the directive to release Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu, as most organisations have extended only moral support to the call.
The bandh, scheduled from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., is unlikely to affect public or private transport, shops and commercial establishments, hotels or eateries. Schools and offices are also expected to function as usual. Essential services such as healthcare, grocery stores, pharmacies and banks are expected to remain functional. Transport services are also likely to operate normally, as autorickshaw and cab unions have extended only moral support to the bandh.
On Wednesday, Mr. Nagaraj said that the Kannada Okkoota had decided to go ahead with the bandh and that he would not call it off. He also said they would carry out a rally from Town Hall to Freedom Park at 11 a.m.
“From 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., the bandh will be effective. Mandya will be entirely shut down, and complete support will be received in Hubballi, Dharwad, Raichur and Ballari,” he said.
While Mr. Nagaraj had initially said that the bandh in the State was in protest against the Cauvery Water Management Authority’s (CWMA) directive to release water to Tamil Nadu, he clarified on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) that the bandh was also intended to highlight all major irrigation and development issues, including the Kalasa-Banduri and Mekedatu projects.
As a precursor to the event, Mr. Nagaraj’s group held a demonstration with “brooms” at Majestic Bus Stand on August 12 before being escorted away by the police.
Meanwhile, Kannada outfit Karnataka Rakshana Vedike (KRV), which has been at the forefront of several protests in the state, has said that it is not extending support to the bandh. Dinesh Kumar, organising secretary of KRV, said the bandh would not solve the issue, but a legal battle would, which the government was pursuing.
Rudramurthy of the Auto Rickshaw Drivers’ Union and Tanveer Pasha of OTU both told The Hindu said they were only extending moral support to the bandh, as stopping operations would disrupt the lives of lakhs of people.
Emphasising that they support the State’s lawful efforts to secure Karnataka’s rightful share of water for drinking and irrigation purposes, K. Radhakrishna Holla, president of the Karnataka State Travel Operators Association, said they were not extending support to the bandh, but only moral support to the cause.
“Our transport, tourism and service sectors are directly connected with the daily needs of the public. In an internationally recognised city like Bengaluru, continuity of transport, tourism, hospitality, business and other essential services is extremely important,” he said.
Educational institutions to remain open
Meanwhile, private schools, including those affiliated with the Karnataka Associated Management of Schools (KAMS), have withdrawn their earlier advisory regarding the closure of schools in connection with the ‘Cauvery Bandh’, citing the loss of academic days.
“As a symbolic gesture of solidarity, school management representatives, teaching staff and non-teaching staff may wear a black ribbon or black strip on the day of the bandh without disrupting academic activities,” said D. Shashikumar, general secretary, KAMS.
P.C. Rao of the Bruhat Bengaluru Hotels Association also said that the association was extending only moral support, citing food as an essential service.
Police warn against bandh
Bengaluru police have warned against forced shutdowns and road blockades. In a statement, the police said several organisations had called for the bandh, while others had informed the Bengaluru City Police that they were not supporting it. The police said citizens have the democratic and fundamental right to express their views and hold peaceful protests within the framework of the law. However, they stressed that the rights of those who do not wish to participate must also be respected.
“No individual or organisation should force, threaten or compel anyone to participate in the bandh,” the police said, warning against the forced closure of shops, establishments and institutions, obstruction of traffic, and compelling people to participate in protests against their will.
Precautionary security arrangements have been made across Bengaluru, with adequate police deployment, patrolling and security measures at important and sensitive locations.

stories.headline: The long wait for a woman Minister in Karnataka
stories.deck: Inducting a woman into Cabinet has not been a priority of the government
stories.bodyText:
The Karnataka Legislature’s monsoon session will begin on August 13 with an ignominious first in recent history: a Cabinet with not even a symbolic representation of women.
The last fortnight has been marked by endless squabbles over Cabinet expansion and portfolio allocation, with intense arguments on ways to ensure caste and regional representation. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and party functionaries have made multiple trips to New Delhi to consult with the high command, and spent much energy trying to placate “powerful” leaders who are miffed over being denied Cabinet berths or over not getting what are described as “plum portfolios.”
However, women’s representation has clearly not been regarded as an issue worth breaking a sweat over. When asked by the media why not a single woman was included in his 33-member Cabinet, Mr. Shivakumar candidly admitted that there was “no urgency” in the matter, while casually assuring that the one vacant place would be filled by a woman. In fact, it was in an equally casual manner that Gayathri Shanthegowda, the lone woman who was in the Congress high command’s approved first list of Ministers, disappeared before the swearing-in ceremony, as the urgent demands of other powerful interest groups took over.
This situation is nothing short of ironic for two reasons: Congress has nationally been vociferously arguing for 33% women’s reservation, without encumbering it with delimitation or any other riders. At the State level, the Congress government has come to power riding on the back of five guarantees, two of which are specifically aimed at women’s empowerment. While the Gruha Lakshmi scheme promises ₹2,000 a month to women heads of eligible families, Shakti offers free travel to women in select buses.
Symbolic representation
The signalling is that while women are very crucial as voters, they are the last priority when it comes to sharing political power. The final electoral rolls published ahead of the 2023 elections showed that women voters outnumbered men in 17 electoral divisions out of the 34 in Karnataka. Naveddu Nilladiddare, a network of feminists and women’s rights groups, in a letter to the Chief Minister, put it succinctly: “An all-male Cabinet is not an oversight. It is a political choice. It sends an unmistakable message that women and women’s leadership remain dispensable when it comes to the exercise of state power.”
Interestingly, while there have been multiple street protests by supporters of leaders demanding their induction into Cabinet — foregrounding their caste, region, seniority etc. — there were hardly any protests against the non-inclusion of women in the Cabinet. There was some feeble noise in Belagavi in north Karnataka over Lakshmi Hebbalkar, who handled the Women and Child Development portfolio under the Siddaramaiah-led government, being dropped, but none on the larger question of women’s representation. Brahmins not being represented in the Cabinet grabbed more attention than women being denied a place.
The history of electoral politics in Karnataka shows that women’s share in political representation has always been abysmal, much like the rest of the country. In the 2023 Assembly elections, out of a total of 2,613 candidates, 185 were women. Of them, 10 were elected (with one more added in bypolls), which constitutes about 4.5% of the total Assembly strength. In the first two elections in Karnataka in 1957 and 1962, the share of women’s representation stood at 6.25% and 8.65%, respectively, the latter being the highest ever. Since then, the share has fluctuated, with the 1972 election seeing not even a single woman elected to the Assembly out of the 28 who contested. This is all the more striking in a State which was a pioneer in giving 50% reservation to women in local bodies.
The representation of women in Ministry too has been symbolic across parties, with the highest being four when the late S.M. Krishna was the Chief Minister. Women are often given what are regarded as “light weight” portfolios such as Women and Child Development or Kannada and Culture.
No doubt Mr. Shivakumar will stick to his promise of filling the one vacant berth with a woman, but that will not go beyond what it has always been — a symbolic gesture — in the absence of a system that makes representation count.

briefs.headline: Mobile phone found in former MP Prajwal Revanna’s Bengaluru prison
briefs.bodyText:
A mobile phone was allegedly found in the possession of former Hassan MP Prajwal Revanna, who is serving a life sentence for rape at the Parappana Agrahara Central Prison in Bengaluru.
The phone was found during a surprise inspection conducted by Central Crime Branch (CCB) officials in the prison complex on Tuesday afternoon, sources said.
According to sources, the mobile phone was found in the barrack where Prajwal is lodged. The discovery has raised questions about how a prohibited electronic device reached the possession of a high-profile convict inside the high-security prison.
The incident has brought renewed scrutiny on security and surveillance measures inside the Central prison. Allegations of VIP treatment and special facilities being extended to influential inmates at Parappana Agrahara prison have surfaced in the past.
Prajwal, who represented the Hassan Lok Sabha constituency, was convicted in a sexual assault case and sentenced to life imprisonment by a court.
Director General of Prisons Alok Kumar said that one Android phone was seized from Prajwal’s barrack, and Assistant Superintendent Iranna Rangapur has been suspended for dereliction of duty, while a show-cause notice has been issued to the Superintendent of Police, Bengaluru Central Prison.
Sources said prison authorities had searched Prajwal’s barrack on August 6, but the search team could not find any contraband item then. The phone was found on August 11 during the CCB’s five-hour search covering various high-profile prisoners.
Also Read : Rape and punishment: On the life sentencing of Prajwal Revanna
CCB has lodged a complaint at the Parappana Agrahara Police Station, and an FIR has been registered under Section 42 of the Karnataka Prisons (Amendment) Act, 2022, and Section 323 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), naming Prajwal Revanna and an undertrial prisoner Prathap Rai, arrested in a POCSO case, as accused.
Seized phone had social media, streaming services
According to the complaint filed by M.L. Subramanya Swamy, Police Inspector, Narcotics Control Bureau, CCB, during the search officials found a mobile phone, a charger, a blue pocket (electronic) notebook, and a pen drive.
When the prisoners in the room were questioned about the phone, former MP Prajwal Revanna reportedly claimed the notebook belonged to him, while Prathap Rai, an undertrial prisoner, claimed ownership of the mobile phone, charger and pen drive.
Prathap Rai allegedly told the officials that he used the mobile phone occasionally to contact his relatives and lawyer. Prajwal reportedly said he had borrowed the phone from Prathap Rai and used it to contact his relatives and lawyer.
The mobile phone was found to have Facebook, WhatsApp, Instagram, Netflix, Prime Video, and other applications. The applications were password-protected. Both prisoners reportedly told officials that they did not know the passwords.
The seized articles were confiscated in the presence of witnesses.

briefs.headline: DG Prisons orders probe into source of mobile phone used by Prajwal Revanna inside Bengaluru jail
briefs.deck: Director-General of Prisons and Correctional Services Alok Kumar has ordered a departmental inquiry to trace the source of the mobile phone and SIM card allegedly used by former Hassan MP and convicted sexual assault accused Prajwal Revanna inside Bengaluru Central Prison at Parappana Agrahara.
briefs.bodyText:
Director-General of Prisons and Correctional Services Alok Kumar has ordered a departmental inquiry to trace the source of the mobile phone and SIM card allegedly used by former Hassan MP and convicted sexual assault accused Prajwal Revanna inside Bengaluru Central Prison at Parappana Agrahara.
Describing the incident as “very unfortunate” and serious in nature, he said preliminary findings revealed that the SIM card had been active since this March, raising concerns over how the device and communication facilities were accessed inside the high-security prison. It was found that during the raids some prison staff may have tipped off the inmates before the raids and search operations to save them.
The inquiry will focus on identifying those responsible for smuggling mobile phones and other electronic devices into the prison and determining whether prison staff facilitated their use.
Despite the installation of high-tech signal jammers, the use of mobile phones inside prisons continues to pose a challenge, the DG said. Authorities have identified certain blind spots where mobile signals remain accessible and have requested the telecom department to rectify the issue.
Officials have also found that some of the active SIM cards being used inside the prison were connections issued in Andhra Pradesh. The Prisons Department has sought details from the telecom operator and indicated that accountability would be fixed after verification of the subscriber information and the service provider will be booked .
The DG confirmed that Prajwal was not wearing the prescribed prison uniform at the time of the CCB raid.
Soon after the CCB operation, prison officials conducted extensive searches across the jail, including the barrack housing actor Darshan and other high-profile inmates, but no additional contraband was found.
According to department data, nearly 300 mobile phones have been seized from prisons across Karnataka since the beginning of this year. Officials suspect that several more devices may still be operational inside prison premises despite repeated crackdowns.
The departmental inquiry is expected to examine security lapses, the effectiveness of existing surveillance and jamming systems, and the possible involvement of prison personnel in facilitating the entry and use of prohibited devices.

briefs.headline: Karnataka Cabinet: On the eve of Monsoon Session, portfolios finally allocated
briefs.deck: The portfolio allocation from the Governor’s Office came on the evening of August 12 as the Ministers huddled to strategise for the Legislature session commencing on August 13, 2026
briefs.bodyText:
After days of deliberations — amid hectic lobbying for portfolios and attempts by Congress legislators to get inducted into the Cabinet — the D.K. Shivakumar-led Congress government finally managed to allocate ministries on the eve of the Monsoon Session to 19 newly inducted Ministers. Two senior Ministers, who had expressed unhappiness over earlier allocations, were also given different portfolios.
Senior Minister K.H. Muniyappa, who was earlier miffed at being continued as Food and Civil Supplies Minister after he had sought Social Welfare, has managed to prevail over the party leadership. Ramalinga Reddy, who was upset at not being given Bengaluru Development and instead given Water Resources Ministry, has been allocated Forests, Ecology and Environment. Besides, Health and Family Welfare Minister U.T. Khader has been given the additional responsibility of Minority Welfare, Haj and Wakf.
The Chief Minister has retained the Law and Parliamentary Affairs besides all other unallocated portfolios.
At a time when the State is facing challenges over deficit rainfall and the farming community is in distress, the Agriculture portfolio has been given to P.M. Narendraswamy, and the Major and Medium Irrigation portfolio has gone to N. Cheluvarayaswamy, both hailing from Mandya district. Puttaranga Shetty, from Chamarajanagar district, has been allocated Animal Husbandry and Sericulture.
The portfolio allocation from the Governor’s office came on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) evening as the Ministers huddled to strategise for the legislature session commencing on Thursday (August 13, 2026). The newly inducted Ministers with their portfolios will have their first full Cabinet meeting on Thursday (August 13, 2026) afternoon.
The allocation comes even as the government will be headed to the session without a woman Minister, though the Chief Minister has promised that the remaining one berth will be filled by a woman legislator. briefs.headline: Bengaluru: Deadline for vacant site owners to clean properties extended to August 22

The Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) has extended the deadline for owners of vacant sites to clean up accumulated debris and overgrown weeds on their properties from August 15 to August 22, following requests for additional time.

briefs.headline: These Bengaluru stores make classics a decor choice for all
briefs.deck: Now, bring home a masterpiece without worrying about the overhead costs
briefs.bodyText:
If you have wistfully pored over classic works of art and sighed at their unavailability or ever wondered if prints ordered online would be worth it, here are two places in the city where you can pick from a multitude of options, and get an idea how they would look in your home.
Peephole to the world
Off a quiet lane in Koramangala, Tallenge is an office-and-store in a nondescript building where Praveen Gupta P and his team are busy sourcing and framing prints of paintings and posters in various sizes. Their range, which can be perused online, is vast. With over 40,000 paintings from old masters such as Da Vinci, Rembrandt and Monet to modernists Munch, Klimt and Amrita Sher-Gil, besides a host of others as well as movie posters, the site is a treasure trove where one can lose track of time.
Tallenge initially began as a platform to promote new talent, but Praveen soon realised not many people support up-and-coming artists, at least not on a commercially viable level. He also found out the hard way that online platforms had made the process of returning products so easy, customers had no qualms in returning original works of art in various states of mutilation.
Sites such as Google Art and Culture as well as the creation of prints do not detract from the importance of the artist or the role of museums. “Instead, museums are witnessing an increase in footfall with young visitors keen to experience art they may have first seen online. The works of long-forgotten or obscure artists come to light, and the value of art appreciates as more people know about it,” says Praveen.
Since art which has been in the public domain for 70 years or more can be accessed by all, the range of art which can be made available commercially is considerable.
Still, Praveen and his team do their due diligence before uploading an image on to their site and while there have been no issues over copyright, he recalls an incident in the reverse. “The grandchild of an artist approached us asking if we had a particular piece in our collection; the woman in the painting was their mother and they did not have a copy for themselves.”
Praveen says this line of work opened up interesting avenues of thought and learning. “News of the sale of an art work at Christie’s could have you going down the rabbit hole of history, geography and interesting trivia.”
“What would compel Hiroshi Yoshida, a Japanese printmaker, or American explorer Edwin Weeks, living at the turn of the century to travel around the world painting? Their works offer a glimpse into life and society in those times and still fetch a handsome price today.”
Weeks’ Two Nautch Girls was sold for close to ₹5 crore at auction earlier this year. “Every painting has a story to tell and are rich in nuggets of information. And it is never ending as there is far more art in the world than one can consume in a lifetime.”
Browsing through the site will eventually get you to their movie posters section, even if that is not your original intent. Over 2,000 posters ranging from classic Indian hits to vintage Hollywood as well as some of their foreign language releases abound; facetious minimalist movie posters complete the segment.
According to Praveen, when Hollywood movies were released in Thailand they came out unofficially which meant there were no Thai versions of the movie poster. “This gave rise to a subculture of hand-painted random posters in Thai. Someone would create artwork, most of them were poor in quality and context as not many knew English there, and then print a few 100 copies to create publicity. Hindi films were similarly promoted in villages and small towns back in the day.”
Today, the original posters are rare, but even prints are worth a pretty sum and are sought by collectors, sociologists, anthropologists and the like, he says.
As part of their services, Tallenge frames and delivers orders if required.
Tallenge is at 663 2nd Floor, 5th Cross Rd, 4th Block, Koramangala. Catalogue of artists and posters available at tallengestore.com
Making a statement
In the heart of the city, tucked away into one of its smaller lanes is Montage. Here, works of art line the walls and are neatly stacked, giving you a chance to browse. Since most of these are reproductions, the sizes range from the standard to customisable and customers can view their options online.
While this gallery on Lavelle Road showcases paintings, murals and more, Arte’Venue serves as the company’s e-commerce platform dedicated to art prints. According to Neeraj Dugar, co-founder of Arte’venue, their website displays the work of more than 5,000 artists worldwide, working with the estates or publishing houses of those deceased.
“We have the requisite licenses to print these, and apart from fixed sizes of which we have four to five variations, we also give customers the opportunity to decorate odd-sized niches with art painted to fit that space.”
Besides reproductions, Montage offers a paper or canvas option for prints. For instance, one can find The Kiss by Gustav Klimt mounted on a round canvas here.
“One can use the customisation tab on the website or come to the store to decide on the medium they prefer. If someone has a fondness for a particular artist we have a team to replicate his masterpieces,” says Neeraj, adding all the artists come from a fine arts background.
“We identify talented artists from across the country who are proficient in specific styles of painting and offer clients options to tweak favourites. That way, customers get exclusive art inspired by the original and as unusual as it may sound, there is a market for this. It also offers many struggling artists a chance at employment even as they wait for their own work to get recognised.”
Old Bengalureans may remember Blue Spade, a fine arts gallery; that was forerunner to Montage which has been in business for over 10 years now. “We realised there was a rather small market for fine arts and while most could not afford it, everybody wanted something for their walls. That is how we began Montage, with Arte’Venue as our online platform.”
Montage also extends curation services as well as mirror framing and interior decoration.
Arte’venue by Montage is at 54, Vittal Mallya Road. Log into artevenue.com for details
Get framed
There is no point owning a cherished print if you do not have a suitable frame to offset its beauty. While most stores offer the ubiquitous frames in neutral shades of black, white, metallic and wood tones, Van Gogh’s Arts & Frames gives you the chance to add a pop of colour to your wall art.
From the outside, it seems unlikely this unassuming store on Swami Vivekananda Road, would offer anything other than the tried and tested. Yet, pista green, bright red, royal blue and candy yellow are few of the many frame hues available here.
Started by 1992 in Abdul Aziz, Van Gogh’s is now run by his son Abdul Jaleel MK and business partner Yusuf K, who say they offer clients close to 1,600 frame styles. “We originally set up shop on Shivajinagar’s Central Street, but at one point, there were around 14 frame makers in the area. It was getting too crowded so we moved to this location in 2002,” says Abdul Jaleel.
The shop, which opens out on the road, is small and bustles with staff nimbly stepping around framed art to attend to customers. The walls and worktables showcase many coloured frames which are a welcome change from the usual staid shades found in most places.
Van Gogh’s site has a small selection of wall art where customers can place orders for prints and frames, with a provision for video calls when one may not be able to visit the store as well as limited delivery options, though Abdul admits the in-person experience is quite often preferred by both parties.
“Apart from regular glass, we have non-reflective options and museum-grade sheet glass that offers UV protection for framed art work. Our teak and rosewood frames are highly sought after too,” he says.
Van Gogh’s Art & Frames is at Trinity Church complex, Swamy Vivekananda Road, opposite Lido Mall. Details available at vangoghartsandframes.com

stories.headline: Food prices push up retail inflation to 4.45% in July
stories.deck: Food Inflation Rises To 5.52% From 5.32% A Month Ago
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Retail inflation inched up to 4.45% in July on expensive kitchen staples, including onion and ginger, even as price rise remained above the Reserve Bank's median target for the second consecutive month, according to govt data.
The consumer price index (CPI)-based retail inflation was 4.38% in June.
Data showed transportation costs rose to 4.4% from 4.3%, while inflation in restaurant prices went up 7.7% from 6.9%
The July reading is the highest since the new series, with base year 2024, came into effect in Jan.
Food inflation in July rose to 5.52% from 5.32% in the preceding month, according to CPI data released by the National Statistics Office (NSO).
Inflation in onions increased significantly to 22.54% in July from 4.73% in June. The rate of price rise in ginger shot up to 83.62%. Inflation in garlic also rose significantly.
On the other hand, inflation in potatoes, ladyfinger, peas and tomatoes remained negative.
Earlier this month, Reserve Bank Governor Sanjay Malhotra said higher inflation was mostly on account of fuel and food, with few signs of generalisation of price pressures so far.
Core inflation, excluding precious metals, continues to be benign.
As projected earlier, Malhotra said headline inflation is expected to rise further in the near term and peak in Q3 2026-27, primarily due to food and fuel prices, before moderating thereafter.
The central bank has projected CPI inflation for 2026-27 at 5%, marginally lower than its June estimate.
The govt has mandated the Reserve Bank to ensure retail inflation remains at 4%, with a margin of 2% on either side.
The NSO data further showed that while the national average inflation was 4.45% (provisional) in July, the corresponding CPI rates for rural and urban areas were 4.84% and 3.96%, respectively.
Telangana recorded the highest inflation at 6.32%, while Mizoram (1.84%) recorded the lowest in July, according to the NSO data.
Dipti Deshpande, senior director and principal economist, Crisil, said July brought some relief on the inflation front as food inflation saw a slower rise and non-food inflation remained steady. agencies

stories.headline: New RBI rules may end loan spread tinkering
stories.deck: To Standardise Rate Setting Across Banks, NBFCs
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Lenders may no longer be able to tinker with loan spreads over the benchmark rate to offer new borrowers better deals than existing customers. Draft RBI rules seeking to standardise interest-rate setting across banks, NBFCs and cooperatives require lenders to maintain the spread between the benchmark rate and the loan rate for at least three years.
The proposed framework standardises interest calculation across lenders. Interest on advances will have to be charged on monthly rests, except for specified agricultural advances, and calculated on a daily reducing balance basis using the actual/actual day-count convention.
Smaller lenders will get exemptions from some of the requirements.
For floating-rate loans, the benchmark reset frequency for major lenders cannot exceed three months and must remain fixed for the tenor of the loan. The draft also sets common parameters for spread components and requires non-credit risk components to remain unchanged for three years.
A credit risk premium can be changed only when there is a documented change in the borrower's credit profile following a comprehensive review. Other components of the spread cannot be increased before three years from the first disbursement or the last revision. Lenders can reduce these components earlier for customer retention only on a non-discriminatory basis. 
Loans also cannot be priced below the applicable benchmark.
For commercial banks, floating-rate personal loans and floating-rate loans to MSMEs will continue to be linked to an external benchmark. Banks can use the repo rate, treasury-bill yields, SORR or benchmarks published by FBIL.
Internal benchmarks such as MCLR will have to follow a stricter methodology. MCLR must be based on a three-month moving average of the annualised weighted average cost of fresh domestic deposits and borrowings. The calculation must be system-generated and independently verifiable.
For NBFCs, cooperative banks, RRBs and AIFIs, linking floating-rate loans to an external benchmark will remain optional. These lenders can link such loans to internal or external benchmarks.
Smaller lenders will get exemptions from some of the requirements. RCBs with deposits of up to Rs 1,000 crore, Base Layer NBFCs and Tier 1 and Tier 2 UCBs will not have to comply with the three-month maximum reset frequency or the three-year freeze on revisions to non-credit risk components of spreads.
The methodology used to calculate internal benchmarks will also have to be made publicly available. Loan agreements will have to specify the benchmark, reset periodicity and reset dates.

stories.headline: Govt revises ACC PLI timelines for Ola Electric; unlocks up to ₹7,240 crore
stories.deck: The MHI revision is much more than a timeline extension. The approval secures a full five-year PLI window through CY2031 for Ola Electric's 20 GWh allocation and unlocks up to ₹7,240 crore in cumulative PLI incentives, the company said in a statement
stories.bodyText:
Ola Electric Mobility Ltd. on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) said the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) has approved revised timelines under the ACC production-linked incentive scheme for Ola Cell Technologies Pvt Ltd (OCT), its wholly owned subsidiary.
The MHI revision is much more than a timeline extension. The approval secures a full five-year PLI window through CY2031 for Ola Electric's 20 GWh allocation and unlocks up to ₹7,240 crore in cumulative PLI incentives, the company said in a statement.
Disbursements will be made quarterly, beginning next quarter, creating a recurring incentive stream as Ola Electric scales its cell business, it added.
Ola Electric currently has 2.5 GWh of installed cell-manufacturing capacity, with a further 3.5 GWh under installation.
The company will reach 6 GWh by the end of the current quarter, achieving the initial installed-capacity milestone well ahead of the revised December 2026 timeline.
The MHI decision has effectively extended the original timelines by two years. Lithium cells are becoming a foundational technology across electric mobility, energy storage, drones, robotics and next-generation industrial systems, Ola Electric said.
Building these capabilities in India will strengthen the country's energy security and technology independence while creating a globally competitive domestic battery ecosystem, it added.
Ola Electric is building a multi-chemistry cell platform spanning NMC and LFP technologies, supported by indigenous R&D, increased localisation of battery materials, improved manufacturing yield, and closed-loop material recovery.
Bhavish Aggarwal, Chairman and Managing Director, Ola Electric, said: "The revised timeline is more than an extension. It transforms the economics of our cell business by converting an earlier milestone overhang into a five-year, quarterly PLI opportunity of up to ₹7,240 crore." He further said, "We hadn't factored any incentives into our business projections after overshooting the original timelines. Ola is now well ahead of the government's revised schedule, and enables us to access the full potential of ₹7,240 crore and receive disbursement as soon as next quarter." At the company's annual Sankalp event on this Independence Day, Ola Electric will unveil its broader energy product roadmap-including Shakti, Mahashakti, and the next phase of its energy platform.

briefs.headline: Who next? Tata Steel MD’s name does the rounds after Chandrasekaran steps down
briefs.deck: 'Not prepared', P 26
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: For the past few decades, change of guard at Bombay House has often been accompanied by a large dose of drama.
N Chandrasekaran's sudden announcement has added to the uncertainty of the past few months, when battles within Tata Sons and Tata Trusts boards brought back memories of yesteryears.
The question now uppermost in everyone's mind is: who will replace Chandra? Tata Sons has a fair bit of time to plan the transition, since Chandra is expected to remain chairman till Feb 2027, .
Under Tata Sons' articles, the chairman is selected by a five-member committee. Three members are nominated jointly by Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT), one by Tata Sons board, and the fifth is an independent member chosen by the board. SRTT cannot currently participate because it is unable to convene trustee meetings following a directive from the Maharashtra charity commissioner - a complication for Chandrasekaran's succession and a new wrinkle in Tata Sons' planning.
Chandrasekaran abruptly announced his decision “not to offer himself for reappointment when my term ends on Feb 20, 2027”
Noel Tata could have stepped in as interim chairman. He is due to retire from the boards of other Tata group companies in Nov under the group's policy, which sets 70 as the retirement age for non-executive directors. 
He will continue as a Tata Sons director as he is a Trusts nominee, and Trust nominees are not subject to a retirement age.
When Cyrus Mistry was removed as chairman in 2016, Ratan Tata stepped in as interim chairman at 78, four years after stepping down as chairman himself. The board subsequently appointed Chandrasekaran to bring stability. Noel may not be able to take the same route this time. Tata Sons' amended articles bar the Tata Trusts chairman from also serving as Tata Sons chairman - a rule introduced in 2022. Ratan Tata was the last person to hold both positions.
Among the names in circulation for the top job is TV Narendran, 61, managing director of Tata Steel. A Tata veteran who joined the group in 1988, Narendran has spent his entire career at Tata Steel and led the company since 2013.
Noel Tata, Tata Sons director and Tata Trusts chairman, is vice-chairman of Tata Steel, and Narendran has described the late Ratan Tata as a mentor who guided the steelmaker through a difficult period of transformation.

briefs.headline: India's Godrej Consumer logs worst day in 6 years as sudden CEO exit heightens execution concerns
briefs.bodyText:
Shares of India’s Godrej Consumer Products plunged more than 11% on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) and posted their steepest fall in over six years as CEO Sudhir Sitapati’s abrupt exit fuelled concerns over strategic execution at the consumer goods company.
The maker of Cinthol soaps named finance chief Aasif Malbari as CEO and managing director on Tuesday(August 11) after Sitapati resigned, just three months after his reappointment for a five-year term.
Godrej Consumer’s shares, which slipped to a three-year low, settled 11.2% lower at 910 rupees in their busiest session since May 2021. The stock was the top loser on the FMCG index , which ended 0.7% lower.
Analysts said the sudden leadership transition puts greater focus on the execution of Godrej Consumer’s growth plans, with improved performance in its core brands seen as key.
This comes after Godrej Consumer Executive Chair Nisaba Godrej on Tuesday (August 11) said the company needed greater “execution rigour”, particularly in online sales, digital marketing and liquid vaporizers.
“An abrupt change is never liked by the market,” said Amit Purohit, senior vice president at Elara Securities, adding that investors would monitor execution of the company’s plans before they regain confidence in the stock.
HSBC downgraded Godrej Consumer to “hold” from “buy” and cut its target price to 1,120 rupees from 1,260 rupees, citing greater uncertainty, while Goldman Sachs and Nomura retained “buy” ratings but lowered their targets. NEXT PHASE
Despite Sitapati’s pivotal role in shaping the company’s 2040 vision, the management highlighted other areas where execution could improve, including the use of AI and effective digital marketing, Jefferies said in a note.
Vision 2040 is Godrej Consumer’s long-term growth strategy focused on expanding its addressable market, entering new categories and targeting faster-growing segments.
“Bringing in an experienced internal CFO to steer the company through margin and cost pressures shows how important profitability and operating efficiency are in today’s environment,” said Agamjeet Dang, CEO of executive search firm Executive Access.
Malbari, who joined Godrej as CFO in 2023, has more than three decades of experience across the consumer goods and automotive sectors, including leadership roles at Hindustan Unilever and Tata Motors.

briefs.headline: Further lab test results awaited, says Aviation Ministry after reports of flight captain testing positive for drugs
briefs.deck: Both pilots have been removed from flying duties pending an inquiry into an incident where an Air India flight dropped mid-air, leaving 24 persons injured before it stabilised
briefs.bodyText:
The Ministry of Civil Aviation said on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) that it was awaiting the drug test results for the captain of an Air India flight that dropped about 300 feet mid-air last week, injuring 24 passengers and crew members.
The incident on the Airbus A320 took place shortly after it took off on August 4 from Phuket, Thailand to New Delhi while carrying 137 passengers, including three infants and eight crew members. The aircraft later stabilised and landed safely in New Delhi, officials said.
The incident has come under intense scrutiny after some media reports, quoting unnamed sources, said that the captain may have tested positive for marijuana in a follow-up drug screening.
Following the incident, both pilots underwent routine screening for psychoactive substances after the flight landed, the Ministry of Civil Aviation said in a statement. Psychoactive substances include alcohol, drugs or other substances that can affect judgment and alertness.
The Ministry said the captain’s initial test result required further laboratory confirmation and that both pilots were removed from flying duties pending the inquiry.
An official who spoke on condition of anonymity, because he was not authorised to speak to the media, said details of the drug screening would be included in the investigation report once it is completed.
India’s Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau, or AAIB, is reviewing flight data, aircraft systems, maintenance and operational records, medical information, and conducting interviews as part of an independent investigation.
The Ministry said that under international aviation rules, France’s air accident investigation agency, BEA, and aircraft manufacturer Airbus are assisting Indian investigators. They are providing technical expertise, aircraft design information and other documents to help determine what caused the incident, it added.

briefs.headline: SBI uses AI to underwrite nearly ₹1 lakh crore in MSME loans in FY26
briefs.deck: "In FY26, in 12 months, we can underwrite loans up to ₹5 crore, both covering the new-to-bank customers, as well as existing customers. Almost ₹1 lakh crore we were able to underwrite," says SBI Managing Director
briefs.bodyText:
The country's largest lender, State Bank of India (SBI), used artificial intelligence to underwrite nearly ₹1 lakh crore in MSME loans of up to ₹5 crore each during 2025-26, a senior bank official said on Wednesday (August 12, 2026).
"In FY26, in 12 months, we can underwrite loans up to ₹5 crore, both covering the new-to-bank customers, as well as existing customers. Almost ₹1 lakh crore we were able to underwrite," SBI Managing Director Rama Mohan Rao Amara said at the annual FIBAC event in Mumbai.
He added that the bank is also deploying artificial intelligence, including Large Language Models (LLMs), to automate processing of cheques up to ₹10,000.
The use of AI has helped free up the bandwidth of relationship managers, who earlier spent considerable time collecting data and carrying out preliminary analysis, the official said.
Cheques of up to ₹10,000 account for around 25% of the bank's cheque volumes, and the AI model can read the cheque and verify mandatory fields and compliance requirements, the official said.
The bank has now automated processing of such cheques through a STP (straight-through processing) system, with practically no human intervention.
However, SBI has retained a control mechanism under which a dedicated control risk unit reviews a sample of cheques processed by the AI system to identify errors and determine whether the models require further training.
He said AI is being deployed across the customer lifecycle, including credit underwriting, portfolio management, fraud risk management and customer service.
SBI is also using AI-based early warning signals to identify vulnerable exposures before delinquencies emerge, by analysing sector-specific, market and other publicly available information.
On the benefits of AI, the official said quantifying the impact in terms of a defined reduction in the cost-to-income ratio would take time, but the bank was already seeing benefits in terms of customer satisfaction and release of employee bandwidth.

briefs.headline: Yokohama plans to expand tyre production to 6.3 million units

briefs.bodyText:
Japanese tyre major Yokohama said it was targeting double-digit growth in passenger car radial tyres on the back of growing demand for SUVs in the Indian market. It is also planning to increase production from 4.5 million units to 6.3 million units in two to three years, a top executive said.

He said India is the 4th biggest market for Yokohama after Japan, the U.S. and China.
“Our continued investments in manufacturing, technology and premium product development reflect our confidence in the country’s long-term growth,” Mr. Mantri said.
The company runs two car tyre plants at at Bahadurgad, Haryana and Vishakapatanam in Andra Pradesh.

The company plans to offer the tyres in 32 sizes across 16- to 20-inches, dedicated for crossover and premium SUVs in India. Of these, 17 sizes are currently available, while the remaining 15 will be introduced over the next two to three months.
The range is aimed at vehicles spanning compact SUVs and electric SUVs such as the Maruti Suzuki Brezza, Kia Sonet, Tata Nexon EV, Harrier EV, Mahindra XUV700 and Kia Seltos.

briefs.deck: GNPA ratio improves to 2.7% from 3.3% a year ago, while net interest income rises 10.2% in the June quarter
briefs.bodyText:
Repco Home Finance reported an 8.9% year-on-year growth in its loan book to ₹15,990 crore as of June 30, 2026, while net profit for the first quarter of FY27 increased to ₹114 crore from ₹108 crore a year earlier.
Total income rose 6.1% year-on-year to ₹468 crore during the quarter, while net interest income increased 10.2% to ₹216 crore, according to a press release.
Loan sanctions grew to ₹938 crore from ₹907 crore in the year-ago period, and disbursements increased to ₹843 crore from ₹829 crore.
Housing loans accounted for 70.8% of the outstanding loan book, while home equity products made up 29.2%. Loans to the non-salaried segment constituted 53.5% of the portfolio, with salaried borrowers accounting for the remaining 46.5%. All loans in the portfolio are retail loans, the release said.
Asset quality improved, with the gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio declining to 2.7% as of June 30, 2026, from 3.3% a year earlier.
Gross NPAs stood at ₹427 crore, compared with ₹485 crore a year ago. The net NPA ratio remained unchanged at 1.2%, while net NPAs increased to ₹194 crore from ₹171 crore a year earlier.
Repco Home Finance reported a capital adequacy ratio of 36.13% as of June 30, well above the regulatory requirement of 15%. The company operated through 210 branches and 32 satellite centres across 12 states and the Union Territory of Puducherry.

briefs.headline: N Chandrasekaran steps down: How power struggle at Tata group is deepening with exit of Ratan Tata’s key allies
briefs.deck: The battle for influence within the Tata Group after the death of former chairman Ratan Tata in 2024 has led to the exit of several senior leaders who were closely associated with him, altering the leadership dynamics at India's largest business conglomerate.
briefs.bodyText:
N Chandrasekaran
’s decision to step down as Tata Sons chairman after his current tenure ends in February 20207 has brought to light the power struggle within the Tata group.
His decision represents a major leadership change at Tata Sons and leaves the board with the task of selecting a new chairman while differences within Tata Trusts remain unresolved.
The succession process is expected to be closely watched because Tata Sons occupies the centre of the Tata Group's ownership structure, while Tata Trusts, through its majority shareholding, continues to wield significant influence over the conglomerate's long-term strategic direction.
The battle for influence within the Tata Group after the death of former chairman 
Ratan Tata
 in 2024 has led to the exit of several senior leaders who were closely associated with him, altering the leadership dynamics at India's largest business conglomerate, according to a PTI report.
Also Read |
‘Don’t pay attention to gossip, conspiracies you hear’: What N Chandrasekaran told Tata Sons staff
The latest prominent departure came on Wednesday, when N Chandrasekaran, popularly known as Chandra, announced that he would not seek another term as chairman of Tata Sons after his current tenure ends on February 20, 2027.
His decision comes after the gradual exit of two of Ratan Tata's long-time confidants, Vijay Singh and Mehli Mistry.
Heart of the dispute
The centre of the leadership tussle is Tata Trusts, which owns about 66 per cent of Tata Sons and holds decisive control over the holding company of the salt-to-semiconductor conglomerate.
The Tata Sons board currently comprises six members: Chairman N Chandrasekaran, Tata Trusts Chairman Noel N Tata, Tata veteran and Tata Trusts Vice-Chairman Venu Srinivasan, Group Chief Financial Officer Saurabh Agrawal, and independent directors Harish Manwani and Anita Marangoly George. Noel Tata, the half-brother of Ratan Tata, took over as chairman of Tata Trusts in 2024 following Ratan Tata's death.
The composition of the Tata Sons board has changed considerably amid the broader governance dispute involving Tata Trusts. Vijay Singh, the former defence secretary who served as a Tata Trusts nominee on the board, stepped down in 2025, while independent directors Ajay Piramal and Ralf Speth also retired, the PTI report said.
N Chandrasekaran's journey at Tata Group: Transformation and challenges
Tata Sons: Who owns it?
Tata Sons, the holding company of the Tata Group, is majority-owned by a group of philanthropic trusts, which together hold around 66 per cent of its equity. The largest shareholders are the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust with a 27.98 per cent stake and the Sir Ratan Tata Trust with 23.56 per cent. Together, the two trusts own a combined 51.54 per cent of Tata Sons.
The remaining trust-held stake is spread across several other entities, including the JRD Tata Trust (4.01 per cent), Tata Education Trust (3.73 per cent), Tata Social Welfare Trust (3.73 per cent), RD Tata Trust (2.19 per cent) and the Sarvajanik Seva Trust (0.10 per cent).
Since October 2024, Noel N Tata has chaired Tata Trusts while also serving as a non-executive director on the Tata Sons board. The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT), the single largest shareholder in Tata Sons, recently appointed Neville Tata, Noel Tata's son, and former Titan chief Bhaskar Bhat as trustees for three-year terms. Venu Srinivasan is also a trustee of SDTT and serves as its vice-chairman.
The Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) has emerged as the focal point of the recent governance dispute within the group. Vijay Singh, who served as its vice-chairman and as a trustee of Tata Trusts, has stepped down and will not seek another term when his tenure at SRTT expires on August 14, 2026, though he will continue as a trustee of SDTT. Venu Srinivasan has also played a key role as an SRTT trustee, while Mehli Mistry, a long-time associate of Ratan Tata, has exited the trusts.
Also Read | 
From trainee to Tata chairman: The remarkable rise of Ratan Tata’s pick N Chandrasekaran
How the dispute has deepened
The governance dispute within Tata Trusts deepened through 2025, with trustees splitting into two opposing camps. One faction coalesced around Noel Tata, while the other was led by Mehli Mistry and included trustees Pramit Jhaveri, Jehangir HC Jehangir and Darius Khambata, the PTI report said. Mistry's association with the extended Shapoorji Pallonji family, which owns about 18.37 per cent of Tata Sons, added a further dimension to the conflict.
In the early stages of the dispute, Noel Tata was supported by Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh as differences sharpened over board appointments and governance matters raised by the Mistry-led group.
Vijay Singh who served as a Tata Trusts nominee director on the Tata Sons board, later stepped down from the board after opposition from the Mistry faction.
The main point of contention has been the composition of the Tata Sons board and the distribution of seats on the board of the holding company that oversees the 156-year-old Tata Group, whose operations span hundreds of businesses, including around 30 listed companies.
The disagreement escalated to the point of attracting the Centre's attention. As tensions over the governance of Tata Trusts intensified, Noel Tata, N Chandrasekaran, Venu Srinivasan and trustee Darius Khambata met Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in October last year.
Also Read | 
Standoff with Noel Tata: What led to N Chandrasekaran’s exit as Tata Sons chairman
Tata Sons listing: Point of Disagreement
One of the biggest areas of disagreement within the Tata Group has centred on the future of Tata Sons and whether the holding company should eventually be listed on the stock exchanges.
Noel Tata has opposed the idea of a public listing, whereas Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh have openly backed listing Tata Sons, the promoter holding company of the Tata Group, PTI reported.
According to reports, Chandrasekaran did not agree to Noel Tata's request that he categorically rule out the possibility of taking Tata Sons public.
The differing views on the group's long-term ownership and governance framework have further strained relations between the trustees and the management of Tata Sons.
Another source of friction was Noel Tata's reported proposal to appoint his son, Neville Tata, as a trustee of the Sir Ratan Tata Trust, a move that Srinivasan and Singh are understood to have opposed.
The divisions within the trust also disrupted its functioning, with meetings of the Sir Ratan Tata Trust being cancelled twice this year, first in January and again in May, for different reasons.
Mehli Mistry distances
Mehli Mistry, who had consistently voiced governance-related concerns across various Tata Trust bodies, gradually began distancing himself from entities within the Tata Group.
Among his most notable decisions was stepping down from the board of RNT Associates Pvt Ltd, the personal investment company and family office founded by Ratan Tata.
Following Mistry's exit, differences between Noel Tata and Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh became increasingly pronounced, with the future governance and ownership structure of Tata Sons emerging as the principal areas of disagreement.
In April this year, Venu Srinivasan resigned as a trustee of the Bai Hirabai Jamsetji Tata Navsari Charitable Institution, citing other business commitments as the reason for his decision.
The latest leadership change came on Tuesday when Vijay Singh resigned as a trustee of the Sir Ratan Tata Trust, just a day before N Chandrasekaran announced that he would not seek another term as chairman of Tata Sons.
Singh chose not to seek an extension of his tenure, which ends on August 14. However, he will continue to serve as a trustee of the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust.
Also Read | 
Tata group stocks fall up to 4% as N Chandrasekaran steps down as chairman
Why N Chandra decided to step down
According to Chandrasekaran, both the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and the Sir Ratan Tata Trust had unanimously backed a five-year extension of his tenure as chairman of Tata Sons.
He said the recommendation was subsequently endorsed by the Tata Sons Nomination and Remuneration Committee and approved by the board before being placed before directors at the February 24 board meeting. However, the proposal did not go through after one board member withheld support.
"In the absence of unanimous support, I chose to defer the decision," Chandra said.
With the matter remaining unresolved for six months, Chandrasekaran said it had become important to provide certainty over the group's leadership for employees, investors, partners and other stakeholders, particularly as Tata Sons is executing several strategic projects.
He said he had therefore informed the board that he would not seek reappointment after his current term ends on February 20, 2027, and urged directors to identify his successor at the earliest to facilitate a smooth transition.

stories.headline: Pakistan javelin thrower Arshad Nadeem to skip Diamond League meet in Lausanne
stories.deck: Arshad’s long-time coach, Salman Butt, said the javelin thrower was presently training in Lahore but would soon leave for South Africa, where he will train for a few weeks under his coach, Terseus Liebenberg, and local trainers
stories.bodyText:
Pakistan's Olympic gold-medallist javelin thrower Arshad Nadeem will skip the Diamond League meet in Lausanne this month to focus on preparing for another international event and the Asian Games in Japan this year.
Arshad’s long-time coach, Salman Butt, said the javelin thrower was presently training in Lahore but would soon leave for South Africa, where he will train for a few weeks under his coach, Terseus Liebenberg, and local trainers.
“He has decided against competing in the Diamond League meet this month as he wants to be ready for the Asian Games,” Butt said.
Arshad didn’t qualify for the top eight in the finals of the recent Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, where Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage eventually took the top spot with a throw of 89.75 metres, while India’s Neeraj Chopra and Yash Vir Singh took the second and third spots respectively.
It was the first time two Indians had featured on the javelin throw podium after a final.
Arshad was scheduled to compete in the Lausanne Diamond League on August 21 along with other big stars, including Chopra, Julian Weber and Anderson Peters.
However, he will now miss the competition and travel to South Africa for a training camp.
The 28-year-old will train in Potchefstroom for two weeks, a venue where he has previously completed two training stints ahead of the 2022 Commonwealth Games and 2024 Olympics, where he won gold medals.
After his training stint in South Africa, Arshad is expected to compete at the World Athletics Ultimate Championships, to take place in Budapest from September 6 to 14. He will then participate in the Asian Games.
Butt said Arshad was just waiting for his visa to leave for South Africa.
This year, Arshad has struggled in two international meets and came in for sharp criticism after finishing ninth in the CWG finals.

stories.headline: Chelsea sign defender Chavarria from Rayo Vallecano on five-year contract
stories.deck: Financial ⁠details of the deal were not disclosed, but British media reported that ‌Chelsea had paid an initial £16.3 million ($22.02 million) with a ‌further £1.7 million in add-ons for ‌the ⁠28-year-old
stories.bodyText:
Chelsea have signed Spanish left back Pep Chavarria from Rayo Vallecano on a deal until 2031, the Premier League club said on Wednesday.
Financial details of the deal were not disclosed, but British media reported that Chelsea had paid an initial £16.3 million ($22.02 million) with a further £1.7 million in add-ons for the 28-year-old.
"This is a dream for me as Chelsea are one of the biggest clubs in the world. It is a big opportunity but I am prepared and will work hard to help the team achieve success," Chavarria said in a statement.
Chavarria played for Figueres, Olot and Zaragoza in the lower tiers of Spanish football before joining Rayo Vallecano in 2022. He made 125 appearances in all competitions and played a key role in their run to the UEFA Conference League final last season.
The defender's signing boosts new Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso's options at left back following the departure of Spaniard Marc Cucurella to Real Madrid.
Chelsea, who finished 10th last season, begin their new Premier League campaign at London rivals Fulham on August 24. ($1 = 0.7404 pounds)

stories.headline: FC Goa crash out of AFC Champions League Two after 0-3 loss
stories.deck: FC Goa’s AFC Champions League Two campaign ended with a 0-3 loss to Turkmenistan’s FC Arkadag. After a goalless first half, Arkadag scored three times in 17 minutes after the break to seal victory. FC Goa will now compete in the AFC Challenge League, while Arkadag advance to the Champions League Two group stage, with the draw on August 18.
stories.bodyText:
FC Goa
’s AFC Champions League Two campaign came to an end after they suffered a 0-3 defeat against Turkmenistan’s FC Arkadag in the preliminary round at the Arkadag Stadium on Wednesday.
The Indian side could not find a goal after a goalless first half, while Arkadag came out strongly after the break and scored three times in just 17 minutes.
The result means FC Goa will now continue their Asian campaign in the AFC Challenge League, the continent’s third-tier club competition.
Arkadag take control after break
Arkadag looked dangerous from the beginning and regularly used the wings to create chances. FC Goa goalkeeper Bob Jackson Raj was kept busy and made several important saves to keep his side in the contest.
He denied Begench Akmammedov from close range early on and quickly recovered to stop Abdy Basimow’s follow-up attempt. Raj was called into action again in the 26th minute, making a diving save to prevent Bashimov’s header from a corner from crossing the line.
FC Goa created their best first-half chance from a set-piece in the 42nd minute. Francisco Feuillassier’s delivery found Sandesh Jhingan, but the defender’s glancing header went away from the target.
Arkadag also missed a late chance before the break when Rahman Myratberdiýew’s overhead effort went over the bar.
Three goals end FC Goa’s hopes
Arkadag finally broke the deadlock in the 58th minute. Yazgylych Gurbanov’s cross found Didar Durdyyew in a crowded penalty area, and his effort slipped through Raj’s hands and crossed the line.
Rahman Myratberdiýew doubled the advantage seven minutes later after collecting a loose ball, racing into the box and calmly finishing past the advancing goalkeeper.
Arzuwguly Sapargulyyew then sealed the victory in the 75th minute with a superb free-kick into the top-right corner.
FC Goa struggled to respond as Arkadag comfortably protected its lead. The Turkmenistan club’s win takes them into the AFC Champions League Two 2026-27 group stage, with the draw scheduled for August 18 in Kuala Lumpur.
FC Goa, meanwhile, will now turn their attention to the AFC Challenge League.

stories.headline: East Bengal run riot in extra time to reach AFC Champions League Two group stage
stories.deck: The home side appeared set to exit the competition after trailing 0-1 with only 14 minutes of regular time remaining.
stories.bodyText:
East Bengal staged a late comeback to beat Kuwait's Al Arabi SC 4-1 after extra time and qualify for the group stage of the AFC Champions League Two at the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata on Wednesday.
The home side appeared set to exit the competition after trailing 0-1 with only 14 minutes of regular time remaining.
Jay Gupta then brought East Bengal level in the 90th minute, giving the hosts a chance to turn the match around.
East Bengal carried that momentum into extra time and took control of the game.
Captain Mohammed Rashid put the Kolkata side ahead in the 108th minute to make it 2-1.
Substitute David Lalhlansanga then extended East Bengal's lead in the 117th minute.
Rohit Danu completed the comeback by scoring in the first minute of stoppage time in extra time, sealing a 4-1 win for East Bengal.
The victory sends East Bengal into the group stage of the AFC Champions League Two.
East Bengal, who won the Indian Super League last season, their first top-flight triumph in 22 years to qualify for the continental competition, will now enter the West Region group stage in the continent's second tier club football.
The group phase will feature 16 teams playing in a round-robin format with home-and-away fixtures.

briefs.headline: Praggnanandhaa beats Sindarov in Sinquefield Cup
briefs.deck: Praggnanandhaa was the star of the day all the way as the Indian claimed his point inch-by-inch in the endgame arising out of a queen pawn opening
briefs.bodyText:
Indian Grandmaster R Praggnanandhaa crashed through the defences of Javokhir Sindarov in a second round match to register his first victory of the Sinquefield Cup, the penultimate event of the Grand Chess tour, here.
The star of the day was Praggnanandhaa all the way as the Indian claimed his point inch-by-inch in the endgame arising out of a queen pawn opening.
Sindarov, who will be up against world champion D Gukesh later this year for the world crown, chose just an equal endgame that should have been a perfect draw for him.
But then what he possibly did not account for was Praggnanandhaa’s tenacity. It paid off in the end for the Indian as from what the computer was claiming to be a drawn endgame turned in to a winning one in no time. The game lasted as many as 95 moves.
With Praggnanandhaa reaching 1.5 points from his two games, the overnight leader Fabiano Caruana of United States was the only one to end matters peacefully with a draw against Anish Giri of Holland.
The Dutchman is known for his deep opening preparation and he did not disappoint his fans but Caruana was well armed with his black piece.
After just one decisive result in the first round, the equation changed dramatically with four decisive results in round two as Levon Aronian of United States showed his class to beat Vincent Keymer of Germany, Wesley So of United States proved superior against Jorden Van Foreest of Holland and Maxime Vachier-Lagrave, the consistent Frenchman, defeated Savian Sameul of United States.
There are five leaders sharing the top spot on 1.5 points apiece with seven rounds still to be played in the 475000 USD prize money tournament.
The three Americans, Caruana, Aronian and Wesley, are up in front along side Praggnanandhaa and Vachier-Lagrave, and it remains to be seen who is going to call the shots.
